definition: Over-fitting occurs when a model learns the detail and noise in the training data to the extent that it negatively impacts the performance of the model on new data.
details: Over-fitting occurs when a model learns the detail and noise in the training data to the extent that it negatively impacts the performance of the model on new data. Under-fitting occurs when a model cannot capture the underlying trend of the data and fails to perform well even on the training data.

explainer.lead: Over-fitting and under-fitting are the two classic ways a model fails: one memorizes noise, the other misses the trend. Both matter because they signal the model will not perform well where it counts.

tiers.eli5: Over-fitting is memorizing the answers to last year's test; under-fitting is not studying at all and failing even the practice questions.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers diagnose the pair by comparing training and validation error curves and respond with regularization or more capacity respectively. A common pitfall is treating high training accuracy as success without checking held-out performance.
tiers.paperLevel: Over-fitting: the model learns detail and noise in the training data to the extent that performance on new data suffers. Under-fitting: the model cannot capture the underlying trend and performs poorly even on the training data.

explainer.example: A model with 99% training accuracy but 60% validation accuracy is over-fitting; one with 55% on both is under-fitting.
